Risk of Rain Returns is a beautiful remake of a roguelike classic. And for better or worse, it is remarkably consistent with the original. It excels in many of the ways the original did. The survivors (and enemies) are remarkably creative and dynamic. The gameplay is classic risk of rain, teeth-grindingly tough until you get the hang of it, with more diverse items than the vast majority of roguelikes out there. And the pixel art is beautiful. All of the sprites, stages, and logbook entries are beautifully done. Theres an entirely new gamemode which features some of the most fun and creative uses of characters and their abilities (while ALSO having their own little creative pixel art icons.) The game has all of the remarkably positive aspects of risk of rain 1, but simultaneously, it carries some of the first game's major flaws into the new iteration. It solves one or two glaring issues (like having to kill ALL the enemies before entering a teleporter), but still lacks some of the important developments which the second entry in the series added. The absence of 3d printers, the bazaar, lunar items, stage choices, and other elements strip the game from really ANY kind of strategy. The game plays and feels great but the player has no real choices in what kind of build or items they want to center around. This makes most runs, while fun, generally somewhat repetitive. Secondly, the game does not get any updates, meaning the few glitches, bugs, and imbalances are here to stay. 

Risk of Rain Returns is a solid 8/10 which clings to the first game's identify so dearly that it misses a few important developments which could have helped the game to achieve an entirely new level of quality.
